item.title: Plateau Attack: Death toll rises to 19
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The death toll from an attack on Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), a community in Jebbu Miango, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, has risen to 19 following the death of three persons who were rushed to hospital after the incident. The attack reportedly occurred on Wednesday night, November 25, and continued into the early hours of Thursday, November 26, 2026, throwing the community into confusion, fear and panic. A resident of the community, Moses Monday, who confirmed the casualty figure on Thursday, said 16 bodies were recovered at the scene, while three other victims died after being taken to hospital. Monday said: “This is evil. I can confirm that 16 bodies have so far been recovered at the spot, with an additional three who died after they were taken to the hospital. These evil men will not rest.” Another resident, Nuhu Fidelis, who also confirmed the attack, described it as another assault on a neighbouring community in Jebbu Miango. Fidelis said: “Yes, in the early morning of today, Thursday. Last night, November 25, 2026, a Christian neighbouring village, Tafi-Gana (Cando Zrreci), in Jebbu Miango, Bassa LGA, Plateau State, was attacked again. Many innocent people lost their lives.” He condemned the killings and called on the government and security agencies to take urgent measures to protect residents. Another resident, Paul Nehemiah, who said he lost a close relative in the attack, described the killings as wicked and unprovoked, adding that residents had been living in fear following repeated attacks. Nehemiah said: “We are tired of burying our people. These are farmers, women and children who did nothing to anyone. How long will this continue? We are calling on the government to rise up and save us.” Rita Joseph, whose family fled the village during the attack, said community members could no longer sleep peacefully because of persistent security threats. She said: “We ran into the bush with our children.” The residents appealed to the Plateau State Government, the Federal Government and security agencies to deploy more personnel to Miango and surrounding communities to prevent further attacks. They also urged the authorities to take decisive action to bring the perpetrators to justice and restore confidence among residents. Efforts to obtain comments from the Plateau State Police Command spokesman, SP Alfred Alabo, and his counterpart at Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, were unsuccessful, as they had yet to respond to inquiries by our correspondent as of the time of filing this report. The post Plateau Attack: Death toll rises to 19 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations
item.description: ‎Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, has received the report of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry established to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of 37 artisanal miners while in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger State Command. ‎The Governor received the report from the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, at the Government House, Minna, where he reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to implementing its recommendations. ‎Governor Bago expressed appreciation to the Commission on behalf of the bereaved families, the Miners Association and the NSCDC, describing the report as an important document that would guide stakeholders in addressing the circumstances surrounding the tragic incident. ‎He commended Justice Muhammad and members of the Commission for their dedication, sacrifices and thoroughness throughout the investigation, assuring that the government would carefully consider the findings and recommendations. ‎The Governor also disclosed that a copy of the report would be forwarded to the Presidency for reference, underscoring the importance of the investigation and its outcome. ‎Earlier, the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, thanked the Governor for the confidence reposed in the panel and the opportunity to serve. ‎He explained that the Commission received nine memoranda, conducted public hearings and carried out inspection visits to two mining sites, two NSCDC offices and the General Hospital in Minna as part of its investigation. ‎Justice Muhammad said the evidence and facts gathered during the proceedings formed the basis of the Commission’s findings and recommendations. ‎He further explained that the report was presented in three volumes for ease of reference, with Volume One containing the findings, observations and recommendations; Volume Two containing the records of proceedings; and Volume Three comprising all exhibits tendered before the Commission. ‎In his remarks, the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Nasiru Mu’azu, described the deaths of the 37 artisanal miners as a grave incident in the history of Niger State. ‎He commended Governor Bago for demonstrating commitment to the rule of law by establishing the Judicial Commission of Inquiry to investigate the incident and ensure that the circumstances surrounding the deaths were thoroughly examined. ‎Mu’azu assured that the Ministry of Justice would carefully study the report and advise the government on appropriate actions and the next steps to be taken. ‎ ‎ The post Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tinubu housing projects deliver over 26,000 units, 525,100 jobs, APC-PCC says
item.description: …As MOFI implements N1 trillion mortgage programme By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC said on Thursday thst the President Bola Tinubu administration has facilitated the financing and delivery of over 26,000 housing units and generated 525,100 real estate construction jobs nationwide in the past three years. Spokesperson of the council, Dele Alake, made the claim in a statement issued in Abuja. According to the statement, the Ministry of Finance Incorporated MOFI, through the MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF), has provided more than N158 billion in mortgage financing to 2,269 homebuyers as of October 31, 2026. The statement said the fund financed properties valued at more than N279 billion, while 695 housing units have received offtake guarantees, “creating a ready market for private-sector property development”. It said 6,620 properties have been listed on the fund’s platform, with 21 financial institutions providing mortgage services across 28 states and all six geopolitical zones. MREIF, a N1 trillion housing finance programme sponsored by MOFI, commenced operations on March 17, 2025, to expand access to affordable mortgages and mobilise private investment in the housing sector. The statement said beneficiaries can access mortgage loans at an interest rate of 9.75 per cent per annum, with repayment periods of up to 20 years and a minimum equity contribution of 10 per cent. It added that the fund raised an initial N250 billion, made up of N150 billion in concessionary Federal Government funding and N100 billion in private commercial investment. “To enable more Nigerians to own homes, President Tinubu’s administration recognises that affordable mortgage loans, reasonably priced developer financing, and local production of building materials are crucial to reducing housing costs and expanding construction activities,” the statement said. On construction, the council said the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development is building 10,328 housing units at different stages of completion under the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme. These include 2,744 units at the Renewed Hope City in Abuja, 2,000 in Kano and 2,084 in Lagos, while another 3,500 units are being developed under the Renewed Hope Estates Programme across 14 states. The Federal Housing Authority FHA, it said, is delivering 3,341 units, including 1,550 units for armed forces personnel in Jabi, Abuja. The Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria FMBN accounts for another 11,294 housing units, comprising 9,076 units financed between 2024 and 2025 and 2,218 units delivered in the first quarter of 2026. According to the statement, the ministry’s housing projects are estimated to have generated 258,200 employment opportunities, while FMBN’s interventions have generated 226,900. item.title: FIFA confirms cyberattack, says hackers stole personal, business data
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FIFA has confirmed a criminal cyberattack that exposed a limited amount of personal and business information, while files linked to its abandoned World Cup stake-sale plan were not accessed. According to Reuters, a person with direct knowledge of the incident said less than 0.1 per cent of FIFA’s total data was affected and no files from the FIFA Forward Enterprise project were accessed. “FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information,” a FIFA spokesperson told Reuters. The football governing body condemned the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data, calling it “a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy”. FIFA did not disclose when the attack took place, how many people or organisations were affected, or what business information was accessed. It also did not say whether any data had appeared online or where it may have been published. FIFA scrapped plans in July to sell private investors a stake in a new unit that would manage its events, including the World Cup. The proposal aimed to raise up to $4.2 billion by selling a 20 per cent stake. The post FIFA confirms cyberattack, says hackers stole personal, business data appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meet Nigeria’s Damilola Bolarinde, crowned Miss International Africa 2026
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian beauty queen Damilola Bolarinde has been crowned Miss International Africa 2026 after representing the country at the 64th edition of the Miss International pageant in Tokyo, Japan. The continental title was announced on Thursday, November 26, a day after the grand finale held on November 25, which featured 73 contestants from different countries. Bolarinde, popularly known as Queen Dammy, secured a place among the Top 20 contestants but did not advance to the Top 10. Her performance at the competition earned her the Miss International Africa title. The achievement adds to her growing profile in the Nigerian beauty pageant industry, having represented Lagos State at the 2025 Miss Universe Nigeria competition, where she emerged first runner-up behind Anambra State representative, Onyinyechi Basil. In April 2026, Bolarinde won the Face of Hope pageant, earning the right to represent Nigeria at the Miss International competition as Miss International Nigeria 2026. She defeated contestants representing Anambra and Rivers states, who finished as first and second runners-up, respectively, at the event held on April 19 at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos. Meanwhile, Elizaveta Kuznetsova of Moldova won the overall Miss International 2026 crown, becoming the first contestant from her country to claim the title. Brittany Feeney of the United Kingdom finished as first runner-up, while Laura Glozarová of the Czech Republic came third. Victoria Kosasieputri of Indonesia and Khánh Như Lê of Vietnam completed the Top Five, finishing fourth and fifth, respectively. Bolarinde’s continental recognition marks another milestone in her pageant career and adds Nigeria to the list of countries represented among the award recipients at the international competition. The post Meet Nigeria’s Damilola Bolarinde, crowned Miss International Africa 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Opposition coalition confirms Monday summit, to adopt 3 key documents
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Coalition for Democracy has confirmed that the Second Summit of Nigeria’s opposition political parties will hold on Monday in Abuja, with participating parties expected to adopt three foundational documents. The coalition is a multiparty platform pioneered by the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Social Democratic Party (SDP). In a statement signed by Salihu Moh. Lukman on behalf of the coalition parties, it said the decision was reached on Wednesday night at the seventh meeting of its Central Leadership Committee. The statement said the leaders reached the decision “following extensive deliberations on the state of the nation, the prevailing political environment and the earlier resolution to suspend campaign activities on day of the Summit”. The leaders, however, made it clear that the suspension does not end inter-party engagement. “The leaders agreed that the suspension of campaign activities does not preclude the continuation of consultations and engagements among opposition political parties on matters of common interest, including electoral integrity, democratic participation and institutional reform,” the statement said. The documents to be considered and adopted are the National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, the Framework for Opposition Unity and the National Reform Programme. They were developed by working groups made up of representatives of the constituent parties after the inaugural summit of August 31, 2026. According to the statement, “the documents set out proposed mechanisms for inter-party cooperation and a framework for addressing national governance challenges.” The coalition leaders also reaffirmed their commitment “to working collectively to safeguard the integrity of the electoral process and protect the sanctity of the ballot across the country”. The coalition invited other opposition political parties to participate in the summit and “contribute to the ongoing consultations”. Three personalities will address the summit on the theme, “The Doctrine of a Necessary Democratic Opposition”. They are the Alaago of Kajola Alago, Ileshan, HRH Oba Oladipo Olaitan; Prof. Ango Abdullahi; and Chief S. N. Okeke. The statement said the summit is expected to bring together “national leaders of opposition political parties, elected representatives, former public officeholders, civil society leaders, representatives of the media, and observers from foreign diplomatic missions in Nigeria”. item.title: 19 years after, Olajumoke’s hostels for disabled students decay
item.description: — Invaded by bedbugs, broken doors, faulty drains — Students seek urgent intervention as AAUA VC promises action By Dayo Johnson AKURE — Nineteen years after former Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council of Adekunle Ajasin University, Akungba-Akoko, Senator Bode Olajumoke, donated two hostels for students with disabilities, the facilities have fallen into a state of disrepair, with residents appealing to the university authorities for urgent intervention. Olajumoke, who visited the male and female hostels he donated in February 2006, expressed dismay at their condition, describing the facilities as horrible and neglected. Conducted round the buildings by the hostel manager, Joseph Aladegbola, the former senator said the living conditions of the students were unacceptable and urged the university management to urgently rehabilitate the facilities. Olajumoke donated the hostels after discovering that the institution had no accommodation specifically designed for students with disabilities. The two buildings, alongside an office for the hostel manager, were commissioned by former Senate President, Senator Ken Nnamani, with the late Governor Olusegun Agagu as guest of honour. They were purpose-built to accommodate students with physical disabilities, with wide doors and toilets and bathrooms designed to allow wheelchair access. However, the hostel manager attributed the poor state of the facilities to inadequate funding, saying the hostels received maintenance funds at most twice a year, an allocation he described as insufficient to address their needs. After inspecting the buildings, Olajumoke visited the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Tomola Obamuyi, where he raised concerns about the level of deterioration. He warned that the unhygienic conditions could trigger disease outbreaks if urgent steps were not taken to address them. Olajumoke said the male hostel was in a worse condition, adding that both buildings had been invaded by bedbugs and required immediate fumigation. He called on stakeholders to work together to improve the living conditions of students with disabilities. One of the students lamented that the rooms, bathrooms, toilets and kitchen were all in a state of neglect. “The institution has neglected the hostels, the toilets are bad, doors and windows falling, all other facilities are in deplorable conditions,” the student said. The student appealed to the university authorities to restore the buildings to the condition they were in when Olajumoke donated them. Also speaking, a former hall chairman, Joseph Agada, urged the university management to prioritise the renovation of the hostels before the situation deteriorated further. Agada called for comprehensive repairs, including the replacement of damaged bathroom and toilet facilities, provision of new chairs and fumigation to tackle the bedbug infestation. “We need the complete renovation of the two hostels, new chairs, the fumigation of the hostels because of the invasion of bedbugs. item.title: Succession Battle: Court issues arrest warrant against Jimmy Odukoya
item.description: By Henry Ojelu A Lagos State High Court sitting in Ikoyi has issued a bench warrant for the arrest of Pastor Jimmy Odukoya over his failure to appear in court in a contempt case arising from the leadership crisis at the Fountain of Life Church. Justice O. Adewunmi-Oshin issued the warrant on Thursday following Odukoya’s absence from proceedings in a suit instituted by the Incorporated Trustees of the church. The judge also directed that the case file be returned to the administrative judge for reassignment. The development followed an earlier order issued on November 18, restraining Odukoya from parading himself as the church’s Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head or interfering with its governance, administration and activities. The order was granted following an application by the church’s Incorporated Trustees. The leadership dispute became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that Odukoya was no longer recognised as its Senior Pastor. The faction cited a review of the church’s constitution and a video recording allegedly containing succession instructions left by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya. According to the trustees, the recording, made in December 2021, showed that the late cleric had preferred Pastor Kunle Areogun as his successor, while assigning Jimmy an administrative role and responsibility for the church’s youth ministry. They claimed the recording was not presented when Jimmy was appointed Senior Pastor in September 2023, following his father’s death. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader pending the establishment of a substantive leadership structure. However, Odukoya rejected his removal, insisting that it was not based on a valid decision of the church’s recognised Board of Trustees. He maintained that his appointment in 2023 was unanimously approved and that he remained the duly appointed Senior Pastor. The dispute also resulted in a suit at the Federal High Court in Lagos, where Odukoya and the church’s Incorporated Trustees challenged the validity of resolutions allegedly taken by some members of the board. The suit named his sister, Pastor Tolu Odukoya, and seven other church members as defendants. Speaking during a church service on November 22, Odukoya said he had heard about the restraining order but had not been served with the court documents. “I heard there was an injunction against me. I heard, but I have not seen it, and I have not been served. They said that there was no substituted service. Legally, I have not been served,” he said. He also reassured members of the congregation, declaring: “You know there is no Fountain without you. You are Fountain of Life, and as long as you would have me, I will continue to speak for you.” The Fountain of Life Church was founded in 1992 by the late Pastor Taiwo Odukoya and his wife, Bimbo. item.title: Atiku weaponises poverty for campaign; Obi runs social media algorithm — Bwala
item.description: Daniel Bwala, Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Policy Communication, has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of exploiting poverty to attract voters, saying the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) relies on what he described as the “weaponisation of poverty’s algorithm” for political engagement. Bwala also accused the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, (NDC) Peter Obi, of relying heavily on social media engagement to sustain his political popularity, insisting that online activities and large crowds at rallies were not reliable indicators of electoral strength. He spoke on the Naija Unfiltered Podcast while reacting to questions about whether Tinubu was worried by the growing support for Atiku in the North ahead of the January 16 presidential election. Bwala dismissed the crowds at Atiku’s campaign rallies as insufficient evidence of widespread voter support, arguing that the former vice-president had a history of attracting large audiences during campaigns without translating such gatherings into electoral victories. “I am an advocate from day one that numbers in rally is not a proof of popularity. I even cautioned people from our own side that if we go to a place and everywhere is filled, let us not project it as a strength, because we dey on the street we know how people are gathered in campaigns and Atiku is a master in gathering people when it comes to campaign,” he said. Recalling Atiku’s presidential contest against former President Olusegun Obasanjo, Bwala said the former vice-president gained significant momentum shortly before the election, with large crowds creating the impression that he could defeat the incumbent. He, however, said the rally attendance did not translate into victory, arguing that grassroots mobilisation and actual voter support were more important than crowd size. “I remember the first time he ran on the platform provided by Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu against Obasanjo. It was within few days to election that he was sort of getting some oxygen. If you see everywhere he goes, rave, rave, rave. Everybody believed he was going to defeat Obasanjo. At the end of the day, what is it?” Bwala said. He said genuine political strength should be measured by a candidate’s ability to mobilise voters at the grassroots rather than the number of people attending campaign rallies. Bwala also questioned Atiku’s political structure in the North, asking what support system the former vice-president had in the region, particularly as the party he recently joined had no governor. “But even with the crowd, we have pulled more crowds than him. So what is Atiku Tsunami? What is his structure? Because right now the party he has moved to does not have a governor,” he said. item.title: Bayelsa boat tragedy: Survivors, families recount horror
item.description: …Seven members of one family among victims …Bereaved relatives ask: How do we recover? …Ukubie community appeals for access road By Emem Idio, Yenagoa YENAGOA — Survivors and bereaved families of the November 20 boat tragedy in Bayelsa State have recounted their horrifying experiences, describing how passengers struggled desperately for survival after an overloaded vessel capsized, leaving several people, including children, dead. The boat was conveying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie community in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state for a burial ceremony when the tragedy occurred. One of the survivors, Mrs Lucy Africanist Olugbo, an indigene of Ijo-Gbanraun married in Ukubie, described the ill-fated vessel as an old boat unfit to carry the large number of passengers on board. Olugbo, who was travelling to attend the burial of her husband’s half-sister, said the passengers had initially expected to travel in a speedboat, but a local boat was eventually provided when none was available. She said the boat started making cracking sounds shortly after they boarded, raising concerns among some passengers. According to her, the vessel began tilting from side to side, prompting passengers to shift their weight in the same direction and further destabilising it. She said water had started entering the boat while it was still moving, triggering panic among the passengers. Recounting how she escaped, Olugbo said she secured a bag around her neck before pushing a heavy-set woman forward and jumping into the river. When she resurfaced, she said she saw men, women and children struggling desperately in the water. The survivor also alleged that some youths who arrived in boats, ostensibly to assist in the rescue operation, were more interested in collecting passengers’ phones, money, bags and other belongings than rescuing those struggling in the water. She said she personally witnessed four elderly women and a young woman die in the incident. Another survivor, Mrs Mary Silas, said she travelled with seven members of her household, including her children, younger sister and younger brother. Silas said she became particularly worried because one of her sons could not swim, prompting her to approach the boat driver and appeal to him to stop and allow some passengers to disembark. She said: “The boat was shaking and making strange sounds. Because I was travelling with my son who could not swim, I became very worried. “I approached the driver and told him that there were many children and people who could not swim on board. I told him that since we were close to the riverbank, he should stop and allow some people to come down. “He told me, ‘Okay, madam, I have heard you.’ But to my surprise, instead of stopping, he sped into the middle of the river. item.title: Thailand–Nigeria trade hits $1.88bn in nine months
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Thailand’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Thirapath Mongkolnavin, has said trade between the two countries rose by 104.73 per cent to about $1.88 billion in the first nine months of 2026, compared with the same period last year. Mongkolnavin disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja at a reception marking Thailand’s National Day, Father’s Day and the birth anniversary of the late King Bhumibol Adulyadej. The envoy said Thailand would expand economic and development cooperation with Nigeria and other African countries through its Thailand–Africa Initiative. He said the two countries would mark 65 years of diplomatic relations in 2027, adding that the August visit of Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs to Nigeria and the first bilateral consultations had opened new opportunities for cooperation. He said, “In the economic sphere, our bilateral trade reached approximately USD 1.88 billion during the first nine months of this year, representing a remarkable 104.73 percent increase year-on-year.” Nigeria’s Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Dunoma Umar Ahmed, called for the early conclusion of agreements on investment promotion, air services, visa facilitation and judicial cooperation. Ahmed said the agreements would create more opportunities for trade, investment and tourism. He singled out improved air connectivity as a way to bring businesses and people in both countries closer. He said, “In particular, improved air connectivity between our two countries would serve as a vital link in bringing our peoples, businesses and economies closer together.” Ahmed said the Technical Cooperation Agreement signed during the August visit had opened opportunities for skills development, training and technical exchanges. He identified agriculture, manufacturing, renewable energy, tourism and technology as areas where both countries could expand cooperation. Mongkolnavin said Thailand continued to offer Nigerians scholarships and training through the Thailand International Cooperation Agency’s Annual International Training Course and Thailand International Postgraduate Programme. He said he hoped to use his position as Thailand’s first ambassador to the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, to promote closer dialogue and cooperation between the bloc and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, ASEAN. Ahmed also reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to the safety and welfare of Thai nationals living in the country and thanked Thailand for its support for Nigerians living there. At the reception, the Thai Embassy organised a “Chud Thai” AI photo exhibition to promote Thailand’s traditional attire ahead of its consideration for inscription on UNESCO’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. item.title: ICE arrests undocumented immigrant days after winning $1m lottery
item.description: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has arrested a Salvadoran man in Massachusetts, a week after he won $1 million in a state lottery. The agency’s Boston office said officers arrested Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales in East Boston on Tuesday, following a brief foot chase, according to Fox News. Velasquez-Morales entered the United States in 2013, but an immigration judge ordered his removal from the country the following year. In a statement posted on social media, ICE said his lottery win led to his arrest. The agency also shared a photograph of the Salvadoran man holding an oversized cheque after collecting his prize at the Massachusetts Lottery headquarters in Dorchester, a neighbourhood in Boston. Velasquez-Morales won the prize through the “$2,000,000 50X Cashword” crossword-style scratch ticket game. His name appeared on the cheque as “Ariel Velasquez.” Reacting to the arrest, ICE’s Boston office wrote: “Welcome to the ERO Boston lottery! Where illegal aliens and sanctuary politicians are out of luck, and the law-abiding citizens of New England are always the winners!” In a separate statement, the agency said: “the rights and privileges reserved for American citizens are for American citizens, NOT illegal aliens. The patriots of ICE continue to work around the clock to enforce our nation’s laws and serve the American people.” A 2009 study by the University of Michigan found that 43.9 per cent of undocumented immigrants surveyed participated in lottery or scratch-ticket games. The research, which involved 431 respondents, examined gambling as a form of entertainment and relief among immigrants without permanent legal status. Velasquez-Morales’ arrest came amid renewed attention on the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement, following the departure of another Salvadoran migrant, Kilmar Abrego Garcia, from the United States. item.title: PTAD unveils N5bn health scheme, announces N180bn pension payments
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young LAGOS — The Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD) has unveiled a N5 billion health insurance scheme for retirees under the Defined Benefit Scheme (DBS), while announcing over N180 billion in pension-related payments and interventions in the last two years. The Executive Secretary of PTAD, Tolulope Odunaiya, disclosed this on Thursday at a stakeholder engagement forum in Lagos, where she outlined the Directorate’s achievements in pension administration, including the settlement of inherited pension liabilities, payment of pension increment arrears and introduction of digital reforms to improve service delivery. Odunaiya said the N5 billion intervention culminated in the establishment of the PTAD Health Insurance Scheme (PHIS) for DBS pensioners, which was formally unveiled at the event. “Most significantly, we secured funding of approximately N5 billion for a major healthcare intervention, culminating in the establishment of the PTAD Health Insurance Scheme (PHIS) for DBS Pensioners, which we are unveiling today,” she said. She explained that the scheme was designed to address retirees’ healthcare needs, stressing that their welfare extended beyond the regular payment of monthly pensions. “This initiative reflects our recognition that Pensioners’ welfare extends beyond the timely payment of monthly pension entitlements. Access to free, quality, and reliable healthcare is fundamental to their well-being and quality of life,” she added. On pension liabilities, the Executive Secretary disclosed that PTAD had settled over N91.5 billion in inherited obligations, including N25.05 billion paid to 9,675 former employees of the defunct Nigerian Telecommunications Limited (NITEL) and its mobile subsidiary, MTEL, as final settlement of outstanding entitlements. She also said over N60 billion had been paid in arrears arising from the N32,000 pension increment, benefiting more than 150,000 eligible pensioners. In addition, the Directorate paid over N23.8 billion in arrears arising from pension increments of 10.66 per cent, 12.95 per cent, 13.8 per cent and 20.55 per cent, alongside the implementation of corresponding increases in monthly pensions. On pension harmonisation, Odunaiya said PTAD had disbursed over N5 billion in arrears to more than 64,000 eligible pensioners. She added that over 30,000 pensioners had benefited from monthly pension re-computation, with N3.8 billion paid in associated arrears. The Executive Secretary further announced that 726 retirees had been enrolled on the pension payroll, comprising 508 former employees of the Federal Mortgage Finance Limited (FMFL) and 218 retirees of the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN). The new beneficiaries attract a combined monthly pension obligation of over N41 million, she said. item.title: ‘Completely unacceptable’: Kimmich blasts Bayern over Musiala treatment
item.description: Bayern Munich vice-captain Joshua Kimmich has hit out at the club’s hierarchy for pressuring Jamal Musiala to take a pay cut as he struggles with a neurological condition. Speaking after a Champions League defeat at Lille on Wednesday, the Germany skipper — who is Bayern’s captain with Manuel Neuer currently injured — became the latest to criticise the German giants. “Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than the players, but it is not bigger than the person,” Kimmich said. “It’s completely unacceptable and is not the Bayern way… What’s happening now is something that must not happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible.” In August, Musiala collapsed twice on the field in pre-season games and then revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Musiala played last Friday in his first match since a two-month absence with an unrelated hamstring injury. Moments after the match, long-time club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge said the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form and should accept a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Honorary president Uli Hoeness and current club chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen have made similar statements. Musiala signed a lucrative contract extension in February 2025. According to German media reports, he earns 25 million euros ($27 million) per season, making Musiala the club’s second-highest paid player after Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane. On Sunday, international players’ union FIFPRO accused Bayern of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. Kimmich said he understood the club’s position but was critical of the decision to go public. “I think this is something that should be discussed behind closed doors, something you can address with Jamal’s agent or with Jamal himself,” Kimmich said. Kimmich missed several games in October after the sudden death of his father and said he appreciated the support of the club during that time. “In my own situation, the club was incredibly special. You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out,” Kimmich added. Wednesday’s defeat to Lille ended Bayern’s run as the last club in Europe’s top-five leagues yet to suffer defeat in any competition. item.title: Lagos govt, UNICEF, NGE seek action on child welfare
item.description: By Chioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh LAGOS — The Lagos State Government, United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) and other stakeholders have called for stronger collaboration among government, the media, private sector and communities to address challenges threatening child survival, education and development in Nigeria. The call was made on Thursday at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium in Lagos, themed: “Every Child Alive, Thriving and Learning: A Shared Responsibility.” The event was organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the NGE and Diamond Awards for Media Excellence (DAME), with participation from Airtel Nigeria and other stakeholders. Speaking at the symposium, President of the NGE, Mr Eze Anaba, said ensuring that Nigerian children survived, received quality education and realised their potential was a collective responsibility that should not be left to government alone. Citing a UNICEF report indicating that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, Anaba described the figure as alarming and called for urgent collective action. “In a country of over 200 million people, 18 million-plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming; it’s a collective responsibility,” he said. He challenged media organisations, private sector players, community leaders and parents to assess their contributions towards addressing the challenge. “Have we reminded the government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” he asked. Anaba urged stakeholders to develop an action plan with specific commitments, stressing that annual commemorations must translate into measurable improvements in children’s lives. Earlier, UNICEF Chief of Communication, Advocacy and Partnership, Ms Lone Hvass, said Nigeria’s future would be determined by the decisions made today to protect and invest in its children. She said child survival, education and learning were interconnected, noting that children excluded from school were also denied opportunities for protection, participation and the realisation of their potential. “The media does much more than report on children’s issues. Media helps determine which issues receive public attention, which voices are heard, which assumptions are challenged, and which movements are followed through,” Hvass said. She urged journalists to move beyond episodic coverage and headlines to sustained reporting that connects individual experiences with systemic challenges, provides evidence and exposes gaps in policy implementation. Also speaking, Lagos State First Lady, Dr Claudiana Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu, said the welfare of children required sustained commitment from government, parents, caregivers, development partners and the media. item.title: Champions League top scorers after Matchday 5 (Full list)
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe, Sporting CP striker Luis Suarez and Como attacker Anastasios Douvikas are jointly leading the UEFA Champions League scoring chart after the conclusion of Matchday 5. The trio have each scored six goals in the competition this season, maintaining a narrow lead over a group of players who have found the net five times. Mbappe strengthened his position with a brace in Real Madrid’s 5-1 victory over PSV Eindhoven at the Santiago Bernabeu on Tuesday. Suarez also scored twice in Sporting CP’s 2-2 draw against Manchester United, taking his tally to six goals, while Douvikas remains on the same number. Roma forward Donyell Malen, Manchester City’s Erling Haaland and Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi are next on the list with five goals each. Eight players are tied on four goals, including Paris Saint-Germain duo Ousmane Dembele and Fabian Ruiz, Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes, Borussia Dortmund’s Serhou Guirassy and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane. The other players on four goals are Galatasaray’s Aleksey Batrakov, Stuttgart’s Ermedin Demirovic and Barcelona forward Raphinha. The Champions League Golden Boot race remains open as the league phase continues, with several leading attackers still in contention. item.title: 2027: Violence, Intimidation, Use Of Thugs May Discourage Voters, Amupitan Warns Political Parties
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has condemned violence associated with political campaigns, warning political parties and their supporters against actions capable of threatening peace and undermining the electoral process. Amupitan warned on Thursday as ‎ the Commission and security agencies meet to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 general election. ‎The INEC Chairman stressed the need for political actors to embrace issue-based campaigns, respect opposing views and conduct their political activities within the provisions of the law. Stressing that no political ambition is worth the blood of the citizens ‎He noted that political violence, intimidation and the use of thugs recently witnessed in some states during campaigns could discourage voter participation and weaken public confidence in the democratic process. ‎ Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, and National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, at the meeting. ‎Prof Amupitan said that the commission is working closely with the office of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to identify flash points across the country. ‎He noted that election security remains a collective responsibility, requiring all relevant agencies to work together in addressing violence, intimidation and other activities capable of undermining the credibility of elections. Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu at the meeting ‎Amupitan further emphasised the need for security agencies to operate with professionalism, impartiality and respect for the rule of law, warning that no political interest should be allowed to compromise their constitutional responsibilities. ‎In attendance are the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, the Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, and the Director General of the State Security Service, Oluwatosin Ajayi, among others. ‎The Inspector-General of Police, in his welcoming address, emphasised the need for improved collaboration, intelligence sharing and coordinated security operations to address potential threats to the electoral process. Director General of the State Security Service, Oluwatosin Ajayi, at the meeting. While giving an update on preparations for the upcoming general elections during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), on Wednesday, Amuipitan said that the Commission is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. According to him, INEC has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027. item.title: Mourners Mark Hong Kong Fire Anniversary, Authorities Warn Against ‘Disorder’
item.description: A stream of mourners laid flowers Thursday at the site of a horrific fire that ripped through a Hong Kong apartment complex and killed 168 people a year ago, with authorities warning against “acts of disorder”. The world’s deadliest residential building blaze since 1980 began on the afternoon of November 26, 2025 and raged for two days, gutting seven of Wang Fuk Court’s eight high-rise buildings that were home to some 4,600 people. Authorities in the Chinese territory — where Beijing has cracked down on dissent — appear wary of commemorations taking on a political tone and plan no official memorial. Police on Thursday kept a low profile as mourners laid hundreds of bouquets at a small park beneath the charred shells of the ruined buildings. They included former residents who stood on the same spot a year ago desperately waiting for news of their loved ones. “Families are torn apart, and people died,” said Koey Tam, a housewife and former resident in her 40s who lost her home, adding that they “can never be compensated with a new flat and a huge sum of money”. Smoke rises from apartments after a major fire swept through several blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential estate in Hong Kong’s Tai Po district on November 27, 2025. (Photo by DALE DE LA REY / AFP) The government was “a bit cold” to hold no official memorials, she added. “What can a memorial event possibly affect?” Grace Chan, 69, expressed her frustration at what she called people’s “self-censorship”, telling reporters that “at first, I thought they’d given us a large space” to pay respects to the victims. “Too many Hongkongers remain silent,” she said, as she left a single chrysanthemum at the site. Former resident Dorz Cheung told AFP that he still felt “very, very, very angry” about the government’s response to oversights exposed in the tragedy. “There are still so many emotions… anger, deep sadness, they’re all around.” ‘Seeking Accountability’ A mourner brings flowers to Wang Fu Court in Hong Kong on November 26, 2026, the site of a horrific fire that ripped through seven apartment blocks and killed 168 people a year before. (Photo by Peter PARKS / AFP) The blaze was Hong Kong’s worst disaster in more than seven decades, and a shock to the 7.5 million residents of one of Asia’s safest cities. The city’s number two official Eric Chan said the government will offer help to “lawful” memorial events, but warned against “acts of disorder”. The Chinese government’s Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office spoke this week against attempts to “cause chaos” under the guise of commemorations. According to media reports, some local journalists have faced internal pressure when covering the fire, including to shelve programmes originally scheduled to go on air. A government spokesperson told AFP that as long as it is “within the law”, there are “no restrictions on the freedom to comment and criticise government policies for media outlets”. item.title: Musk To Give Two SpaceX Shares To ‘Every Child In America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk said in a post on X, the social media platform he also owns. The world’s richest person said the share from SpaceX would be transferred next month, while the share from him personally would be transferred in June next year. He did not provide any further details about how the scheme would work. APRIL 30: Elon Musk arrives to court at the Ronald V. Dellums Federal Building on April 30, 2026 in Oakland, California. (Photo by Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) | Benjamin Fanjoy / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP “I recommend holding on to your shares,” Musk said, claiming that SpaceX could “be worth about a million times the current global economy” if it “succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy.” “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them,” he said. In October, Musk promised that every child in the US would receive one SpaceX share, adding that it would be “the first of many.” There are around 73 million people under the age of 18 in the country, according to 2024 data from the Census Bureau. The closing price of one SpaceX share was $127.44 on Wednesday, meaning Musk’s gift would be worth a combined $18.6 billion. SpaceX made its stock market debut in June, raising about $85.7 billion. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the spacecraft central to Musk’s ambition to colonize Mars.
